messages:
sam (support): FYI multiple EU1 customers reporting a spike of 502s and long tail latencies starting ~07:30 UTC. Batches of requests to hosted inference hitting gateway 502s. Seeing customer repro + logs. Link: https://redwood/incident/1758888888 :folded_hands:

maya (oncall): Acknowledged. Which AZs in eu1? Any pattern by route or POP?

sam (support): Mostly eu1-a and eu1-c. Traffic graph: gateway 502 rate ~6x baseline. Auth looks fine (200s from identity). Customers report TCP resets and stalled streams before 502.

li (neteng): Pulling edge eBGP logs and netflow now. Early suspicion: path MTU/fragmentation? I see PMTU ICMPs suppressed on one transit path.

dena (eng-sre): Can you paste a tcpdump/traceroute from an affected gateway host? Also which model routes are failing (hosted-api route ids)?

sam (support): Adding customer repro steps in thread: 1) curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' repeatedly 2) get 502 intermittently after ~800-1500 tokens streamed 3) tcpdump on client side shows SYN/ACK then large POST segments then server sends RST.

li (neteng): Traceroute from eu1-edge1 to customer IP: 
```
traceroute to 203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  edge-eu1-1 (10.1.2.1)  0.5 ms  0.4 ms  0.4 ms
 2  provider-x-pe1 (198.51.100.1)  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.0 ms
 3  transit-y (203.0.113.1)  8.3 ms  8.1 ms  8.2 ms
 4  203.0.113.45  12.7 ms  12.6 ms  12.6 ms
```
But ICMP tests with 1500 MTU succeed, while tcp with big segments sometimes drops. tcpdump on edge shows many `IP frag needed but DF set` messages and occasional `tcp: retransmission` before RST.

dena (eng-sre): That smells like an MTU blackhole between provider-x and transit-y where ICMP blackhole prevents PMTU discovery. Did provider recently change peering?

li (neteng): Checking BGP updates... I see a route change at 07:29:53 UTC: provider-x moved traffic to an alternate next-hop (AS path shortened) with a new interconnect that is using an MTU of 1420. Previous path supported 1500. Provider did not signal CLAMP or send ICMP.

omar (cust-success): Customers are asking for ETA and mitigation. Some are on Dedicated and unaffected. Hosted customers are on edge-eu1 primary.

maya (oncall): Immediate mitigation options: 1) steer hosted-api traffic for eu1 to a secondary peering that preserves MTU (if capacity allows) 2) enable MTU clamp on eu1-edge devices to 1420 3) recommend customer-side TCP MSS clamp as short-term workaround.

deploy-bot: roll request queued: "edge-eu1-mtu-clamp" by maya — awaiting approvals.

dena (eng-sre): I can push a config to clamp MSS on the egress interfaces for edge-eu1. That should avoid fragmentation and restore streams. Will run a canary on eu1-c first.

li (neteng): Confirmed alternate peering capacity at ~60% spare if we steer 30% of hosted-api connections to eu1-b via provider-z. That avoids the low-MTU hop entirely.

maya (oncall): Action plan: (A) Dena to apply MSS clamp on edge-eu1-c canary now and monitor 10m (owner: dena) (B) Li to schedule steering rule to route 30% traffic to provider-z via eu1-b (owner: li) (C) Sam/omar to message affected customers with mitigation and ETA (owner: sam/omar) (D) Neteng to open provider support ticket with provider-x and get confirmation on peering change and MTU (owner: li).

dena (eng-sre): Canary applied to eu1-c: `netconf apply profile edge-mtu-clamp-1420` — watching.

maya (oncall): Monitoring: gateway 502 rate in eu1-c fell from 9/min to 0.8/min in the first 7 minutes. Latency tails improved.

sam (support): Customers on the thread confirm improved behavior after 15 min. Sending note: temporary fix deployed, working on broader steering + provider escalation.

li (neteng): Opened ticket with provider-x: Ticket #PX-91234 — requesting explanation of interconnect change and whether ICMP/PMTU will be signaled. Also asked for rollback.

dena (eng-sre): We'll keep the MSS clamp as medium-term until provider confirms or we catch all routes. Plan to permanently add PMTU monitoring and an alert when `frag needed` ICMPs stop being seen on a path.

maya (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated for now. Will leave thread open for RCA artifacts. Next steps: RCA doc, customer follow-ups, postmortem to include why PMTU alerting didn't fire. Owners assigned in internal ticket. :white_check_mark: 

omar (cust-success): Sharing a canned customer note for review: "We're aware of intermittent 502s in eu1 caused by a downstream provider path change that reduced MTU without signaling. We've applied an edge-level MSS clamp and steered traffic to alternate peers; service stability restored for affected customers. We're working with the provider for a permanent fix and will follow up with the RCA."

sam (support): Thanks everyone. I'll send the customer updates and link postmortem when ready. Closing customer escalation once RCA draft is posted.

maya (oncall): Adding follow-up: create alert rule for `ip_frag_needed_rate > 0.5/min` per edge-pop and `increase in 5xx rate correlated with frag_needed` (owner: dena).

li (neteng): Provider responded: initial note says the interconnect was changed for capacity reasons; they acknowledged MTU mismatch and will roll config to advertise a 1500 path or send ICMPs. Will update ticket PX-91234.

dena (eng-sre): Logged final status: mitigation in place (MSS clamp + partial steering). Monitoring shows steady state. Preparing RCA doc.

sam (support): last update to customers sent at 08:17 UTC. Will attach logs and remediation steps.

maya (oncall): last_message_ts=1758889588 — leaving thread for RCA writeup. Thanks all.
